title: A Pacific temperature contrast gave no clear added 12-month volume forecast gain at 2000-2023 origins
abstract: We tested whether Nino 3 minus Nino 4 improves annual-lead Pacific warm water volume estimates beyond a year of temperature and volume history. We used fixed NOAA GODAS and ERSSTv5 records. Expanding annual ridge fits and inner chronological forecasts used earlier completed targets only. At 288 monthly origins in 2000-2023, the added contrast raised mean squared error by 6.48%. The conditional 95% three-year block interval for error reduction was -19.48% to +4.91%. Baseline and candidate RMSE were 1.06002 and 1.09382 in units of 10^14 cubic metres. Six- and twenty-four-month history checks and a no-trend check also gave intervals that included zero. Thus, a prior six-month gain on these data does not establish a gain at an annual lead. Revised products, few cycles, model choice, same-data follow-up and conditional uncertainty limit inference. No physical cause or operational skill is established. Code, source hashes, aggregate evidence, a figure, and numerical checks support reproduction.

display.caption: Annual-lead volume forecast error reductions and cumulative annual error gains. Intervals use three-year blocks of fixed annual scores. Positive values favor the added temperature contrast.

citations.reason: Nearest six-month test; same source snapshots and related model. Our annual target and new implementation extend the tested scope, without independent data.
